A new report shows an algorithmic pattern appearing across 59 Senate and governor races in the 2026 midterms. 
The analysis shows Republican candidates retained roughly 85% of Trump’s 2024 vote share while Democrats gained the remaining 15%, regardless of how red or blue the state was. The pattern is described as eerily similar to the 2020 “Drop and Roll” theory, in which late night ballot drops and consistent ratios shifted results. The report notes the formula explains about 88% of the variation and held even when individual states were removed. It calls for ballot level audits to examine the numbers.

posts.text:
I normally get blamed for breaking the seal too early by raising the issue of the Woke Right as I did before the election in 2024 (specifically, in October -- maybe I was the October surprise! Lol). I will take a moment to explain myself.

I had realized this problem was coming as early as the beginning of 2021, with confidence by the middle of 2022, and with certainty by late 2023. My own public record of commentary throughout attests to this fact, and my greatest frustration was that nobody wanted to hear it.

In reply, the Woke Right movement, as it started to operationalize in early 2022, had begun making and acting upon specific calls to remove me and my work and influence from American conservative and Republican spheres. Attempts were made to cancel me, also as the record shows. I was also intimidated privately, as the record does not show.

By March 2024, I was in a right state about the issue. Private conversations I did not make public, plus warnings I did make public, started dealing with the question of whether it was even the right course of action to "keep my powder dry" until after the election, which I clearly understood Trump must win (indeed, I made substantial contributions to this effort that cannot reasonably be denied). @SovMichael can, at the very least, attest to these concerns, as he enjoyed or suffered several very long phone discussions with me about exactly this issue: do we start going much harder about the problem now or wait until after the election?

Once Trump survived a direct and close assassination attempt in Butler, PA, on July 13, 2024, and went bandaged into the subsequent RNC to declare JD Vance his running mate, I grew positively alarmed. I didn't know the extent of JD's role in the Woke Right movement, but I knew he was a part of it and that they claimed him, strongly, and defended him in the culty way that goes way beyond the necessary, even over mild criticisms or concerns. I almost resolved to sit the election out and came near a real blackpill.

As the summer progressed, the Woke Right splinter started to activate in full. IT DID NOT WAIT UNTIL AFTER THE ELECTION. You might think it did, but that's an artifact of you not being able to see it at the time. Those of us who could see it could see the blatant activation. The time to say something was drawing close faster than the election was.

It would have been around this time, again as @SovMichael can attest from our private discussions on the issue, that I started forcefully making the case that they were activated and would take advantage of the election no matter how it went:

1) Kamala wins, and they agitate for a civil war that destroys America
2) Trump wins, by the grace of God, and that doesn't happen, so they infiltrate his administration and circles and poison his presidency (or set the stage for a coup).

Something HAD to be said.

But I decided the election was infinitely more important, and that I would hold my tongue, for the most part.

At the end of September, Trump posted the (battle) prayer to Archangel (St.) Michael on the Catholic observance called Michaelmas, which is September 29. I don't know why he did it for certain. I didn't call it out as "Woke Right." Repeat: DID NOT.

Instead, I warned that the weird UN, New Age, globalist esoteric types regard Michael as a dual symbol, so we shouldn't take that symbol as one of our movement without understanding it.

Only once before that did I get so attacked. A narrative was spun that I did a "hates Catholics," which is absurd slander, which even my relatively good friends repeated at me. The cancellation move was swift and total. Fuck everyone involved forever. I have not forgiven you.

Here's some simple logic, though: ACT WOKE, GET CALLED WOKE.

You cannot do a Woke cancellation mob on someone who has survived dozens of them and not understand that they'll recognize it IMMEDIATELY, especially someone who has been tracking and reading your works, your philosophers, and other pointed criticisms of you in exactly those terms, "Woke Right" (cc: @gummibear737 in particular), without them realizing what they're dealing with.

Pretenses ended THAT DAY.

They're Woke Right, and if they're making literally senseless cancellation moves like that, it's rank opportunism to get their opposition (me, in this case) off the table before they made their real moves.

I realized this in real time, and I stopped being silent.

The goal was not to divide the party. It was not to throw the election. It was not to damage the coalition.

The goal was to expose as fully as I could, at a last desperate hour, a problem I had been talking about and being far too careful about for years in the name of holding together something that was already infiltrated and broken.

The splinter itself, the Woke Right, had already divided the party and damaged the coalition. It was going to capitalize in a wicked way on the election, either way it went, and it was systematically removing potential opposition. I was not the first one. There were other prominent reputational lynchings before mine, though those people posed much less threat to their movement than I did. The writing was on the wall, and I could read it.

All I did was read it out loud.

Once Trump won the election and the transition period began, so did what was arguably the most vicious treatment I've ever received in my life. From "friends." "Allies." "Colleagues." Seriously, fuck them all. Forever.

Some of that, surely, is the result of me not only not giving up my campaign but pushing it harder and harder and not giving up. After I hoaxed American Reformer with the Communist Manifesto and got half of Conservative Inc to come out in defense of Marx, Critical Theory, and Postmodernism, the whole movement turned on me like a unit--as a cult.

More to the point, though, as was clear from people I knew in a position to know, who told me as much, my influence was to be completely quarantined away from the administration. There's no doubt it was operational. I've heard and know too much about it.

The Woke Right was a splinter movement conceived at least eight to ten years before I said a word that properly organized and operationalized at least two and a half years before I went hard about it.

It recruited during the Biden years under the branding of a "big tent" and "no enemies to the right," and it operationalized in the lead-up months to Trump's election, either to derail it (or worse) or, at the very least, to opportunize the fact that it's Trump's last term (lol, probably) and therefore to seize the reins of the American conservative and Republican apparatuses after Trump. Deeply cynical. Very organized. Very deliberate. Evil, in my opinion--the only question is HOW evil (which goals are they really after, and for whose primary benefit?).

So, I spoke up. The timing wasn't bad except in that it was both too early and too late. It was too late to do anything about it but still too early for anyone to understand it.

So, that's my piece. The details are horrific. I left almost all of them out.
